{"id":"vouch-xlha.24","title":"check: one bad historical blob aborts check; sync writes no revocations","description":"One unreadable historical version of any registry path aborts check entirely: export, sync, query, keys and status all fail. Sync then writes no revocation file, and because sync refuses a rewind, the registry cannot recover.

Where (HEAD 4237c43): read_blobs at git-vouch:246-251, file_history at 320-321 and registry_history at 1279-1280 raise VouchError for a historical blob over 64 KiB or a non-regular mode (symlink, submodule). check_registry (1429) lets it propagate. cmd_sync calls check_registry at 2388, before the revocation write at 2391.

Reproduced (scratchpad a1/big.sh): commit a 70,000-byte revocations/zz-1.json, delete it in the next commit, then commit a valid revocation of alice's key. check prints "revocations/zz-1.json: a version is not a blob of at most 65536 bytes" and exits 1, with no tiers. export writes nothing, not even the revocation file.

Why it matters: DESIGN.md says "sync writes the revocation file even when check fails on something else, so a revocation always spreads." Once such a commit is merged (a merger who ignored check, or a later git-vouch that tightens a cap), every user's sync fails forever. New revocations never reach anyone, and the only repair is a history rewrite that `_fetch` refuses by design. A malformed working-tree file, by contrast, is just a problem.

Fix: treat an unreadable historical version like an unparsable one. Record it as content that is present but unreadable (record_at already maps unparsable bytes to None), add a problem naming path and commit, and carry on, so the revocation file is still computed and written. Keep failing closed for allowed_signers through `problems`.

new_value: {"notes":"2026-10-23 core-robust: DECISION warning, not problem, for an unreadable past version (directory, symlink, submodule, \u003e64 KiB). Alternative: a check problem (bead's Fix text), failing closed for allowed_signers. Why: history cannot be rewritten (sync refuses rewinds), so a problem would freeze allowed_signers for every user forever; unparsable past versions are already ignored silently by record_at, and this one is at least named. The warning names path and commit on every run. Question for Mark recorded in the unit's output. Also closed the variant: a commit dated beyond datetime (year \u003e= 10000) no longer aborts the history walk; its date is read as 9999-12-31T23:59:59Z and, where check uses it, it is a check problem naming the commit, so sync still writes revocations (test_sync_writes_revocations_past_a_commit_beyond_year_9999). Note for faq3.13: tests/test_export.py::test_tier_ended_at_the_end_of_time_exports exports through a commit dated 9999-12-31T23:30Z; once future commits are check problems that test must instead pin export refusing; the clamp keeps its own unit test test_valid_before_is_capped_at_the_end_of_time."}

unreadable past versions are a warning naming path and commit, out-of-range commit dates a problem, neither aborts; revocations always written (test_unreadable_past_version_is_ignored_and_check_goes_on, test_sync_goes_on_past_an_oversized_version, test_sync_writes_revocations_past_a_commit_beyond_year_9999)
